w_p1: Caption Finder finds the moment a phrase is spoken in YouTube videos. Search a channel, several channels or a list of videos, pick the take you like, and download the trimmed clip.
w_p2: This installer puts Caption Finder in your Applications folder and opens it. It takes less than a minute.
w_li1: Click Continue through the next screens, then Install. Your Mac asks for your password once.
w_li2: Caption Finder opens by itself when it is done.
w_muted: Needs macOS 11 (Big Sur) or newer on a Mac with Apple silicon.
r_p: Caption Finder reads captions from YouTube. Some videos only open for a signed-in viewer, so the app can borrow the sign-in from your browser or use its own. Nothing is sent anywhere except to YouTube.
r_b_1: Open Account & Settings in Caption Finder and choose your browser under Download authentication.
r_b_2: If a red message appears, click Allow access in System Settings. A small Caption Finder window opens beside it.
r_b_3: Drag the icon from the small window into the Full Disk Access list, turn it on, then click Quit & Reopen.
r_o_h: Opera, Vivaldi, or the app's own sign-in
r_o_1: These need no extra permission. For the app's own sign-in, press 1. Sign in to Google, then 2. Connect YouTube, in Account & Settings.
r_end: Then add a channel or a video link, type a phrase, and press Search.
c_p: Caption Finder is in your Applications folder, and it is opening now.
c_open: Open Applications in Finder and double-click Caption Finder.
c_trash_h: If your Mac can't move the installer to the Trash
c_trash: That happens when an earlier Caption-Finder-Installer.dmg is already in the Trash. It's harmless: click OK, then delete Caption-Finder-Installer.dmg from Downloads.
d_subtitle: Caption Finder isn't from the App Store, so your Mac stops the installer once. To let it through:
d_step2: A message says it can't be opened. Click **Done** (not Move to Trash).
d_step3: Double-click the blue button below. In the page that opens, scroll to the bottom and click **Open Anyway**.
d_step4: Confirm with **Open Anyway** and your password. The installer opens: click **Continue**, then **Install**.
d_footnote: On macOS 13 or 14 it's quicker: right-click the installer, choose **Open**, then **Open** again.
